Munnakaya pappu charu/drumstick lentil soup at Tuya’s new menu
Hyderabad’s dining scene has no shortage of options, with new restaurants, familiar favourites and neighbourhood gems competing for attention. But with so much on offer, deciding where to eat can be half the challenge. Whether you’re looking for a leisurely meal, a new cuisine to explore or a good place to catch up over food, here are a few spots worth considering.
Indian winters and pani singhara (water chestnut) share an understated food culture, as do roasted baingan and pakodis. This seasonal food nostalgia inspires Chef Suresh DC’s new menu at Tuya in Jubilee Hills.
The munnakaya pappu charu, with crunchy bits of water chestnut, is a standout. Its peppery lentil base and drumstick broth make it a distant cousin of mulligatawny, while Tuya gives it a refined finish. The creamy consistency and peppery warmth make it an instant favourite.
The thotakura pakoda is a welcome departure from the usual onion variety. “When we have thotakura in so many forms, why shouldn’t we make a pakoda with it? I also wanted to give the palak patta pakoda chaat a break. Hence, thotakura,” says Chef Suresh.
The menu also features mushroom lukmi, a must-try for fans of flaky breads and puffs, along with mutton patti samosa, egg chicken cutlet, mirpakaya bajji and Tank Bund pally masala.
Among the small plates are mushroom paniyaram, Karaikudi jackfruit, mutton uppu kari and miryalu mutton meatballs. Pair these with cranberry nannari sherbet, mango kulki or peach and lychee boba.
Hosa, the modern South Indian restaurant, has launched its Filter Coffee Club in Hyderabad, bringing South Indian filter kaapi into focus through curated tastings, brewing rituals and pairings. Served from a cart on the restaurant’s patio, the experience encourages guests to slow down and savour their coffee rather than treat it as a quick-fix beverage.
Hosa’s ground coffee, blended with chicory, produces a rich decoction that is paired with boiling milk and served in the traditional dabara-tumbler. The coffee is accompanied by South Indian-inspired bites, including onion, egg and chicken bajjis, a murukku sandwich and banana jaggery tea cakes.
The menu also features chef Harish Rao’s much-awaited crispy benne dosas in flavours such as karam podi, karavepaku podi, chicken ghee roast, spinach and corn cheese, and mutton kothu kari.
“The culture of filter coffee in the South is non-negotiable; it’s more than just a beverage. At Hosa, we’ve chosen not to modernise it but to give it the honour it deserves,” says Harish. “We’ve paired these brews with snacks that complement them effortlessly, from our much-awaited benne dosas in varieties such as karam podi, karavepaku cheese podi and mutton kothu kari, to lighter options such as spinach and corn cheese dosa, along with nostalgic favourites like egg and Nellore bhaji. There is something for everyone to enjoy.”
Hosa’s Filter Coffee Club runs from 3pm to 6pm at The Loft, RMZ Nexity, HITEC City.
Tuscany, the Italian speciality restaurant at Trident, Hyderabad, has refreshed its menu with classics and contemporary interpretations. Let me begin with the pizza, which is reason enough for me to return. Hand-tossed and wood-fired, it comes with a sourdough crust that makes all the difference. While the team recommends the Lamb Bolognese pizza, my vote goes to the Bianca. Cheesy, with a hint of truffle oil and topped with enoki mushrooms, it captures the simple pleasures of Italian cooking. For once, I passed up the classic Margherita.
Next came handmade pastas, grills and Italian favourites served as small plates. The cicchetti tiger prawns add to the selection, while the chicken thigh tagliatelle and pan-seared lasagna showcase the kitchen’s attention to detail. A special mention goes to the sauces. The tomato flavour in the chicken thigh tagliatelle, in particular, was pronounced. The chef told me it takes five days to prepare.
The food here steers clear of unnecessary complexity. Executive Chef Gurmeet Bhamra drew our attention to the bread ritual at the beginning of the meal. “Break the bread and take a sniff. This bread, introduced to us by Chef Varun, is made without yeast. The multigrain sourdough quinoa bread takes 48 hours to prepare and is served with herbal garlic butter and thyme-infused olive oil,” he explained.
Tuscany at Trident serves dinner on weekdays, and lunch and dinner on weekends. Monday to Friday: 7pm to 11pm; Saturday and Sunday: 12.30pm to 3pm and 7pm to 11pm. Reservations are strongly recommended.
